knowledge.text: The current diff adds three things to the desklamp skill's general non-desklamp procedure—an 'Admissible Actions' verification clause, a broadened/anti-cycling search step, and a strengthened exact-target/no-substitute step—so its observed response is a joint intervention and cannot be credited to a single clause. Across the 10 verified pairs, task-level success was unchanged: both the pre-edit Parent and the edited Candidate succeeded on 8 tasks, and both hit the 50-step limit on the same two tasks (clean-some-butterknife-and-put-it-in-drawer; put-a-clean-soapbar-in-cabinet). Step counts moved in both directions (Candidate 6 vs 5 in examine-the-pillow-with-the-desklamp and put-some-pencil-on-desk; 11 vs 14 in cool-some-apple-and-put-it-in-microwave), so no clause is isolated and no task-level improvement or regression is demonstrated in this single trial per task.

The newly added 'Admissible Actions' clause requires verifying that a navigation or manipulation command is present in the current admissible list before issuing it, and using a listed direct action on a receptacle when the desired navigation destination is absent. In the observed runs this was not reliably followed: the Candidate still issued navigation commands absent from the admissible list—'go to cabinet 3' from cabinet 1 (Q8:39) and 'go to drawer 8' from drawer 7 (Q7:25)—each returning 'Nothing happens', and the Parent likewise issued an inadmissible 'go to cabinet 1' from cabinet 3 (P8:15). No observed step shows the intended direct-action fallback producing progress, and both put-a-clean-soapbar-in-cabinet runs still ended at the 50-step limit (P8:50, Q8:50).

The revised search step directs the Actor to include visible open surfaces, to prefer a still-untried receptacle type after exhausting one type, and not to re-enter a location just left or repeat a short cycle. The observed response is mixed. Consistent with the clause, in the put-a-clean-soapbar-in-cabinet pair the Candidate visited receptacle types the Parent never reached—bathtubbasin 1 (Q8:3) and sinkbasin 2 (Q8:19)—yet the requested soapbar was not found and both sides still hit the step limit (P8:50, Q8:50). The clause did not break the cycling failure mode: in the clean-butterknife-in-drawer and soapbar-in-cabinet pairs both sides still shuttled among the same receptacles to the 50-step limit (P7:50, Q7:50). In two tasks where the target was found the Candidate spent an extra initial navigation step (Q2:1, Q5:1), giving 6 vs 5 steps, though that inefficiency is not individually isolated.

The revised step 2 states that when the exact requested noun has not been observed, a different but related object must not be acquired, cleaned, cooled, heated, or placed, and that a container holding only a non-matching object should be left unmanipulated. A counterexample appeared in the clean-some-butterknife-and-put-it-in-drawer task: no butterknife was observed, yet the Candidate took a knife from drawer 1 (Q7:9, Q7:13), cleaned it (Q7:17) and moved it to drawer 1 (Q7:19), i.e., it substituted a related object despite the strengthened rule, and the run still ended at the 50-step limit (Q7:50); the Parent substituted the same knife (P7:8, P7:12). In the put-a-clean-soapbar-in-cabinet task the exact soapbar was likewise absent and the Candidate left the visible near-miss soapbottle/spraybottle at cabinet 2 untaken (seen at Q8:7, never taken), but the Parent also abstained there, so that pair does not distinguish the clause.
